title: A flat colimit of finite modules over Noetherian local stages is flat at some stage
statement: Let $(\Lambda,\le)$ be a nonempty directed set. Suppose given, for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] $(A_\lambda,\mathfrak m_\lambda)$ and $B_\lambda$, a local homomorphism $A_\lambda\to B_\lambda$ (it maps $\mathfrak m_\lambda$ into the maximal ideal of $B_\lambda$) and a finitely generated $B_\lambda$-module $N_\lambda$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; and, for $\lambda\le\mu$, local homomorphisms $A_\lambda\to A_\mu$ and $B_\lambda\to B_\mu$ commuting with $A_\lambda\to B_\lambda$ and $A_\mu\to B_\mu$, and an additive map $N_\lambda\to N_\mu$, $x\mapsto\bar x$, with $\overline{bx}=\bar b\,\bar x$ for $b\in B_\lambda$; all transition maps equal to the identity for $\lambda=\mu$ and compatible with composition. Let $A$ and $B$ be the colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the rings $A_\lambda$ and $B_\lambda$ in the category of commutative rings, with the induced ring map $A\to B$, and let $N$ be the colimit of the abelian groups $N_\lambda$, a $B$-module by $\bar b\,\bar x=\overline{bx}$ (and an $A$-module through $A\to B$). Assume that for all $\lambda\le\mu$: (a) the ring map $B_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A_\mu\to B_\mu$, $b\otimes a\mapsto\bar b\,\bar a$, is a localization of $B_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A_\mu$ at some multiplicative subset (a ring map $C\to D$ is a *localization of $C$ at* a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq C$ if every element of $W$ maps to a unit of $D$, every element of $D$ is the image of $c$ times the inverse of the image of $w$ for some $c\in C$, $w\in W$, and $c\mapsto0$ implies $wc=0$ for some $w\in W$); (b) the map $N_\lambda\otimes_{B_\lambda}B_\mu\to N_\mu$, $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,\bar x$, is an isomorphism. If $N$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then there is $\lambda\in\Lambda$ such that $N_\lambda$ is a flat $A_\lambda$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R6 (lemma-colimit-eventually-flat, line 32723), for a system 'as in' Lemma Tag 00QX (lemma-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation, line 32427). Stated with the hypotheses that the proof of 00R6 uses: Noetherian local stages in place of 00QX (2), (3) (essentially of finite type over Z, resp. over A_lambda, which give Noetherian by Lemma Tag 00FN), and 'a localization' in place of 00QX (5) 'the localization at a prime ideal', since the lemma the proof applies, Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness, line 23921), asks only that the target be a localization of the tensor product and that the diagram consist of local homomorphisms of Noetherian local rings. The proof of 00R6 uses Remark Tag 00M6 (Tor_1^R(M,R/I) = Ker(I (x)_R M -> M)), the commutation of tensor products with colimits, and Lemma 00MO.

proof.text: (Notation; restriction to the indices above a fixed $\lambda$.) Write $\alpha_{\mu\lambda}:A_\lambda\to A_\mu$, $\beta_{\mu\lambda}:B_\lambda\to B_\mu$, $\eta_{\mu\lambda}:N_\lambda\to N_\mu$ for the transition maps, $\varphi_\mu:A_\mu\to B_\mu$ for the structure maps, $\iota_\mu:A_\mu\to A$ and $n_\mu:N_\mu\to N$ for the coprojections; $A_\mu$ acts on $N_\mu$ through $\varphi_\mu$, and $A$ acts on $N$ through $A\to B$, so that $\iota_\mu(a)\,n_\mu(y)=n_\mu(\varphi_\mu(a)y)$ (the composites $A_\mu\to A\to B$ and $A_\mu\to B_\mu\to B$ agree, and $n_\mu$ is semilinear). Since $\Lambda$ is nonempty, fix $\lambda\in\Lambda$, write $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_\lambda$ and $\Lambda_{\ge\lambda}=\{\mu\in\Lambda:\mu\ge\lambda\}$. $\Lambda_{\ge\lambda}$ is directed, and every $\nu\in\Lambda$ satisfies $\nu\le\mu$ for some $\mu\in\Lambda_{\ge\lambda}$ ($\Lambda$ is directed). So [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] (1), applied to the cofiltered category $\Lambda^{\mathrm{op}}$ and its full subcategory $\Lambda_{\ge\lambda}^{\mathrm{op}}$, shows: $(A,(\iota_\mu)_{\mu\ge\lambda})$ is a colimit of the system $(A_\mu)_{\mu\ge\lambda}$ in commutative rings, and $(N,(n_\mu)_{\mu\ge\lambda})$ is a colimit of $(N_\mu)_{\mu\ge\lambda}$ in abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. From here on all indices are in $\Lambda_{\ge\lambda}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R6 (lemma-colimit-eventually-flat, line 32723), proof ('Pick some lambda'); the restriction to the indices >= lambda is implicit in 'there exists a lambda' >= lambda'

proof.text: ($\mathrm{Tor}_1$ as a kernel, finitely generated over $B_\lambda$.) Since $A_\lambda$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\mathfrak m=(f_1,\dots,f_r)$. Let $P=\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}N_\lambda$. For $b\in B_\lambda$ the map $(g,y)\mapsto g\otimes by$ is $A_\lambda$-balanced (multiplication by $b$ on $N_\lambda$ is $A_\lambda$-linear, $B_\lambda$ being commutative), so $b(g\otimes y)=g\otimes by$ makes $P$ a $B_\lambda$-module. If $y_1,\dots,y_s$ generate $N_\lambda$ over $B_\lambda$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $g=\sum_ka_kf_k$, $y=\sum_lb_ly_l$, then $g\otimes y=\sum_{k,l}\varphi_\lambda(a_k)b_l\,(f_k\otimes y_l)$, so $P$ is a finitely generated $B_\lambda$-module. The multiplication map $\pi_\lambda:P\to N_\lambda$, $g\otimes y\mapsto\varphi_\lambda(g)y$, is $B_\lambda$-linear, so $K_\lambda=\ker\pi_\lambda$ is a $B_\lambda$-submodule of $P$ (by Remark 00M6, $K_\lambda=\mathrm{Tor}_1^{A_\lambda}(N_\lambda,A_\lambda/\mathfrak m)$; this identification is not needed below). As $B_\lambda$ is Noetherian, $K_\lambda$ is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]; choose generators $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n$ of $K_\lambda$ over $B_\lambda$.

proof.text: (Flatness of $N$.) Let $s:\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}A\to A$, $g\otimes a\mapsto\iota_\lambda(g)a$; it is $A$-linear for $A$ acting on the second factor; let $K=\ker s$. The sequence $0\to K\to\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}A\xrightarrow{s}A$ is exact and $N$ is a flat $A$-module, so by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] $K\otimes_AN\to(\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}A)\otimes_AN\xrightarrow{s\otimes1}A\otimes_AN$ is exact. Under the isomorphisms $(\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}A)\otimes_AN\cong\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}N$, $(g\otimes a)\otimes z\mapsto g\otimes az$, and $A\otimes_AN\cong N$, $a\otimes z\mapsto az$, the map $s\otimes1$ becomes $\omega:\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}N\to N$, $g\otimes z\mapsto\iota_\lambda(g)z$. For $k=\sum_lg_l\otimes a_l\in\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}A$ and $z\in N$ write $k*z=\sum_lg_l\otimes a_lz\in\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}N$ (the image of $k\otimes z$). Hence every element of $\ker\omega$ is $\sum_jk_j*z_j$ with $k_j\in K$, $z_j\in N$. For $\xi=\sum_kg_k\otimes y_k\in K_\lambda$ put $\bar\xi=(1\otimes n_\lambda)(\xi)\in\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}N$; then $\omega(\bar\xi)=\sum_k\iota_\lambda(g_k)n_\lambda(y_k)=n_\lambda\bigl(\sum_k\varphi_\lambda(g_k)y_k\bigr)=n_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(\xi))=0$ (step 1). So for $i=1,\dots,n$ there are finitely many $k_{ij}\in K$, $z_{ij}\in N$ with $\bar\xi_i=\sum_jk_{ij}*z_{ij}$.

proof.text: (The kernel dies in $\mathfrak mA_{\lambda'}\otimes N_{\lambda'}$.) Let $J_{\lambda'}=\mathfrak mA_{\lambda'}$, the ideal of $A_{\lambda'}$ generated by $\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}(\mathfrak m)$; $s_{\lambda'}$ takes values in $J_{\lambda'}$. Let $\theta:P\to J_{\lambda'}\otimes_{A_{\lambda'}}N_{\lambda'}$, $g\otimes y\mapsto\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}(g)\otimes\eta_{\lambda'\lambda}(y)$, and $\chi:Q_{\lambda'}\to J_{\lambda'}\otimes_{A_{\lambda'}}N_{\lambda'}$, $g\otimes y\mapsto\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}(g)\otimes y$ (both $A_\lambda$-balanced); so $\theta=\chi\circ(1\otimes\eta_{\lambda'\lambda})$. On generators $\chi((g\otimes a)*y)=\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}(g)\otimes ay=s_{\lambda'}(g\otimes a)\otimes y$, so $\chi(k*y)=s_{\lambda'}(k)\otimes y$ for $k\in\mathfrak m\otimes_{A_\lambda}A_{\lambda'}$. By step 5, $\theta(\xi_i)=\sum_js_{\lambda'}(k''_{ij})\otimes\eta_{\lambda'\mu}(z'_{ij})=0$. Let $B_{\lambda'}$ act on $J_{\lambda'}\otimes_{A_{\lambda'}}N_{\lambda'}$ through the second factor (as in step 2). For $b\in B_\lambda$, $\theta(g\otimes by)=\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}(g)\otimes\beta_{\lambda'\lambda}(b)\eta_{\lambda'\lambda}(y)=\beta_{\lambda'\lambda}(b)\theta(g\otimes y)$, so $\theta(\sum_ib_i\xi_i)=\sum_i\beta_{\lambda'\lambda}(b_i)\theta(\xi_i)=0$: $\theta$ vanishes on $K_\lambda$ (step 2).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R6 (lemma-colimit-eventually-flat, line 32723), proof: 'Hence we see that Tor_1^{R_lambda}(M_lambda, R_lambda/m_lambda) -> Tor_1^{R_lambda'}(M_lambda', R_lambda'/m_lambda R_lambda') is zero'

proof.text: (Conclusion by the local criterion.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-another-variant-local-criterion] to $R=A_\lambda$, $S=B_\lambda$, $R'=A_{\lambda'}$, $S'=B_{\lambda'}$ with $\varphi_\lambda$, $\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}$, $\beta_{\lambda'\lambda}$, $\varphi_{\lambda'}$ (local homomorphisms of Noetherian local rings with $\beta_{\lambda'\lambda}\varphi_\lambda=\varphi_{\lambda'}\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}$, by hypothesis), the proper ideal $I=\mathfrak m$ (so $I'=J_{\lambda'}$) and $M=N_\lambda$, so $M'=N_\lambda\otimes_{B_\lambda}B_{\lambda'}$. Hypothesis (1) of that node is hypothesis (a) for $\lambda\le\lambda'$. (2): $A_\lambda/\mathfrak m$ is a field ($\mathfrak m$ is maximal), so the $A_\lambda/\mathfrak m$-module $N_\lambda/\mathfrak mN_\lambda$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. (3): let $\phi:M'\to N_{\lambda'}$, $y\otimes b\mapsto b\,\eta_{\lambda'\lambda}(y)$, be the isomorphism of hypothesis (b); it is $B_{\lambda'}$-linear, hence $A_{\lambda'}$-linear, so $1\otimes\phi:J_{\lambda'}\otimes_{A_{\lambda'}}M'\to J_{\lambda'}\otimes_{A_{\lambda'}}N_{\lambda'}$ is an isomorphism, in particular injective. The node's map $I\otimes_RM\to I'\otimes_{R'}M'$, $g\otimes y\mapsto\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}(g)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, followed by $1\otimes\phi$ is $g\otimes y\mapsto\alpha_{\lambda'\lambda}(g)\otimes\eta_{\lambda'\lambda}(y)$, i.e. $\theta$; since $\theta$ vanishes on $K_\lambda=\ker(I\otimes_RM\to M)$ (step 6) and $1\otimes\phi$ is injective, the node's map vanishes on that kernel. The node gives that $M'$ is a flat $A_{\lambda'}$-module; since $\phi$ is an $A_{\lambda'}$-linear isomorphism, $N_{\lambda'}$ is a flat $A_{\lambda'}$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] (for injective $X_1\to X_2$, $X_1\otimes N_{\lambda'}\to X_2\otimes N_{\lambda'}$ is identified through $1\otimes\phi$ with $X_1\otimes M'\to X_2\otimes M'$). So $\lambda'$ is an index as required.

split_report.summary: Read 00R6 (line 32723) and its proof, the system of 00QX (line 32427), 00MO (line 23921) with its proof, 00ML (line 23751) and Remark 00M6 (line 18690); tags checked in tags/tags. The statement (adapted hypotheses: Noetherian local stages, 'a localization') is kept: it is what the proof of 00R6 and 00MO need, and it is what the only citer lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre uses in its steps 5 and 7 (systems R_lambda -> S'_lambda, M_lambda and S^_lambda -> S'^_lambda, M^_lambda). Proof in 7 steps following the source: restriction to the indices >= lambda (colimit-initial-full-subcategory); Ker(m (x) N_lambda -> N_lambda) finitely generated over B_lambda (noetherian-submodule-finite), generators xi_i; A and N are the colimits of the A_mu, N_mu as A_lambda-modules (modules-criterion with algebras-elementwise, rings-zero, modules-elementwise) and m (x)_{A_lambda} - commutes with these colimits (tensor-commutes-with-colimits, 00DD); flatness of N over A (flat-tensor-exact applied to 0 -> K -> m (x)_{A_lambda} A -> A) writes the image of each xi_i in m (x)_{A_lambda} N as a sum of elements k*z with k in K; these descend to a stage lambda' (modules-elementwise, rings-zero), where the xi_i die in m A_lambda' (x) N_lambda', and B_lambda-semilinearity kills the whole kernel; the new node lem-weil-pbc-flat-another-variant-local-criterion (00MO, stated with the Tor_1 hypothesis in kernel form via 00M6, as the existing 00ML node is) with module-over-field-flat gives flatness of N_lambda'. The source's 'Ker(m_lambda R (x)_R M -> M) = 0' and 'tensor commutes with colimits' over the varying rings R_lambda' are carried out over the fixed ring A_lambda, so that the proof stays in the route of sk-thm-p1 (the varying-ring node lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-tensor-varying-rings is of unit sk-thm-reduction). Remark 00M6 is used only inside the new node's statement: the item's proof works with the kernels directly. Not a Mathlib leaf: the searches recorded on the node (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep, local_search) plus a new LeanSearch find no descent of flatness to a stage of a colimit.
